The concept of herd immunity is effectively explained by comparing it to a computer network firewall. Just as a firewall protects a digital network by blocking malicious viruses from spreading between unprotected computers, herd immunity protects a population by stopping the spread of infectious diseases. When a large enough portion of the population is vaccinated or immune, the disease has few hosts to jump to, effectively breaking the chain of transmission and protecting those who are not immune, much like how a secure network protects individual machines that might lack their own specific defenses.
